name: Tadashi Yanai
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2000-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2019)
forbes_bio: Tadashi Yanai built and runs Tokyo-listed retail clothing empire Fast Retailing, parent of the Uniqlo chain.
Fast Retailing's other brands include Theory, Helmut Lang, J Brand and GU.
The company reported net profit of $2.8 billion on revenue of $22 billion for the fiscal year ended August 2025.
Flagship brand Uniqlo has nearly 2,500 stores across 25 countries.
Yanai wants his company to become the world's largest retailer, which means it would have to surpass H&M and Inditex (parent of Zara).
forbes_facts: Yanai resigned as an independent director from the board of SoftBank Group after 18 years, in 2019.
Yanai grew up living above his parents' clothing store in a small town in Yamaguchi Prefecture in southwestern Japan.
Yanai has declared English as the company language at Fast Retailing.
He received the Malcolm S. Forbes Lifetime Achievement Award in October 2025.

name: Diane Hendricks
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2020); SEC insider holdings (2025)
forbes_bio: Diane Hendricks owns and chairs ABC Supply, one of the largest wholesale distributors of roofing, siding and windows in the U.S.
Hendricks cofounded the business with her late husband, Ken, in Beloit, Wisconsin, in 1982. She has chaired it since his death in 2007.
She led ABC to make the two biggest acquisitions in its history, buying rival Bradco in 2010 and building materials distributor L&W Supply in 2016.
The company has over 900 branch locations and had $20.2 billion in 2025 revenues.
Hendricks sold custom homes for a builder before meeting Ken, a roofer.
She has spent millions on local economic development, rebuilding entire blocks in Beloit and bringing in several new businesses to the state.
forbes_facts: A Wisconsin native, Hendricks grew up as one of nine sisters on a dairy farm.

name: Andrew Forrest
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2024); Forbes annual (2007-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Andrew Forrest founded Fortescue Metals Group in 2003. It's an iron ore giant which is now transforming itself into a green energy powerhouse.
In 2022, his privately held Squadron Energy paid an estimated A$4 billion for Australia's biggest wind energy company, CWP Renewables.
Forrest has also promised to spend A$750 million on rebuilding Ukraine's energy and communications infrastructure.
Forrest and his wife Nicola founded Minderoo Foundation, a philanthropic outfit with an A$9.6 billion endowment, focused on everything from gender equality to climate change to rebuilding Ukraine.
Forrest and Nicola announced their separation in July 2023 after being married for more than three decades.
forbes_facts: Known by his schoolboy nickname "Twiggy," Forrest was a onetime stockbroker and keen amateur boxer.
He once tried to make a living as an alpaca farmer and is a descendant of the first premier of the state of West Australia, Lord Forrest of Bunbury.
Australia's biggest philanthropists, in 2023  he and wife Nicola gifted shares worth nearly A$5 billion to their foundation.
In September 2024, he struck a $2.8 billion deal to buy hundreds of electric trucks, excavators and dozers for his iron ore mines.

name: David Siegel
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: David Siegel is the cofounder of Two Sigma, a quantitative investing powerhouse that manages $60 billion.
Two Sigma's largest business is a data-driven hedge fund that absorbs large amounts of information to predict the prices of securities.
Siegel and John Overdeck stepped away from day-to-day management of Two Sigma in September 2024, transitioning from co-CEOs to co-chairmen of the firm.
Born in the Bronx, Siegel is a computer fanatic who got a computer science Ph.D. from MIT and worked at hedge funds D.E. Shaw and Tudor Investments.
Siegel's charitable foundation, Siegel Family Endowment, is focused on technology and society and supports programs such as Scratch, which introduces children to coding.
forbes_facts: Before he started Two Sigma with John Overdeck, Siegel founded his own Internet startup.

name: Daniel Ziff
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Daniel Ziff and brothers Robert and Dirk inherited a fortune that dates back to 1927 when their grandfather cofounded publishing company Ziff Davis.
Daniel's late father, William Jr., built up Ziff Davis, which became best known for such trade publications as PC Magazine and Car and Driver.
The publishing business was sold for $1.4 billion in 1994.
The brothers created Ziff Brothers Investments and greatly expanded their inheritance with hedge funds in the U.S. and in London.
Ziff Brothers Investments ceased operations in 2014; the brothers are reportedly investing with former employees of their hedge funds.

name: John Grayken
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Sunday Times Rich List (2020)
forbes_bio: John Grayken is the founder and owner of Lone Star Funds, a private equity firm based in Dallas, Texas, that focuses on corporate equity, real estate, credit, and other financial assets.
Since 1995, Grayken has raised 25 funds with approximately $95 billion in committed capital.
The assets Lone Star buys are managed by Hudson Advisors, a firm based in Dallas that Grayken owns with over 800 employees and more than $260 billion in cumulative assets managed.
Grayken is from a suburb south of Boston, but he renounced his U.S. citizenship for tax purposes in the 1990s and took Irish citizenship.
forbes_facts: He bought Boston's most expensive condo for $33 million in 2016.
While attending the University of Pennsylvania, Grayken played on the ice hockey team as a defenseman.

name: John Henry
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2009-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: After acquiring a fortune in the early 1980s from his trading firm J.W. Henry & Co., John Henry started building a sports empire.
Henry and his partner Tom Werner bought the Boston Red Sox in 2002 for $380 million and delivered the Sox their first World Series win in 86 years in 2004.
Their Fenway Sports Group owns majority stakes in New England Sports Network and Nascar's Roush Fenway Racing.
Henry also has a stake in Premier League soccer team Liverpool, which won the Champions League in 2019.
He bought the Boston Globe in 2013 for $70 million and in 2017 moved the 145-year-old newspaper back to downtown Boston where it was first founded.
forbes_facts: His wife, Linda Pizzuti Henry, is the CEO of both the Boston Globe newspaper and online healthcare publication Stat News.

name: Luca Del Vecchio
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2023-2026)
forbes_bio: Luca Del Vecchio is one of six children of Leonardo Del Vecchio, the late chairman (d. 2022) of EssilorLuxottica, the world's largest eyeglasses firm.
He inherited a 12.5% stake in his father's Luxembourg-based holding company Delfin after his death, along with her stepmother and six siblings.
Besides EssilorLuxottica, Delfin also owns shares in insurer Generali; banks Monte dei Paschi di Siena and UniCredit; and real estate developer Covivio.
He is one of two children Del Vecchio had with Sabina Grossi, Luxottica's former head of investor relations, along with his brother Clemente.

name: Gwendolyn Sontheim Meyer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Gwendolyn Sontheim Meyer inherited an estimated 8% stake in food giant Cargill.
The heiress spends most of her time on a farm in Rancho Santa Fe, Calif., training horses that compete in show jumping.
Her great-grandfather, W.W. Cargill, the son of a Scottish sea captain, founded Cargill in Conover, Iowa in 1865.
The family still owns roughly 90% of Cargill, which did $154 billion in 2025 sales across food, agriculture, financial and industrial divisions.

name: Georg Nemetschek
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2017-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026)
forbes_bio: Georg Nemetschek is the founder and deputy chairman of publicly traded German software company Nemetschek Group.
He started using design software in his own engineering office in the late 1960s, long before computers became available for personal use.
The company, which serves the architecture, engineering and construction industries, went public in 1999 and has annual revenue of about 1 billion euros.
Nemetschek Group expanded into 3D animation and motion design, securing access to the media industry. Its software has around six million users.
In 2020, Georg launched the Nemetschek Innovation Foundation to support scientific research and artificial intelligence in the construction industry.
forbes_facts: In 1971, he was appointed as a professor at the Munich University of Applied Sciences. He served as dean of the Civil Engineering department from 1977 to 1996.
His son Ralf is chairman of the family's Nemetschek foundation, founded in 2007 to strengthen democracy in Germany.

name: Harsh Mariwala
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun India (2015-2022)
forbes_bio: Harsh Mariwala transformed his family's trading business in spices and edible oils into consumer goods giant Marico.
Marico, which is best known for its Saffola cooking oil and Parachute hair oil, sells in 59 countries.
Mariwala's other interests include Kaya, a chain of skin care clinics.
His son Rishabh has a board seat at Marico and overlooks Sharrp Ventures, the Mariwala family office.
forbes_facts: His uncle Kishore Mariwala, who has a stake in Marico and was also a billionaire, died in 2024.
In 2021, he published Harsh Realities, a book chronicling his entrepreneurial journey, co-authored with veteran business consultant Ram Charan.
Telecom billionaire Rajan Mittal has a board seat at Marico.
